name: North Giziga
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Shay, Erin 2021. A Grammar of Giziga: A Chadic Language of Far North Cameroon. Brill, 399pp (Glottolog MED long_grammar). Paywalled.

new_statements.quote: Le fulfulde est une langue sans tons, alors que le giziga a deux registres tonals (haut et bas). Nos sources giziga ne notent malheureusement pas les tons, sauf à de très rares exceptions.
new_statements.translation: Fulfulde is a language without tones, whereas Giziga has two tonal registers (high and low). Unfortunately our Giziga sources do not mark the tones, except in very rare cases.
new_statements.citation: Tourneux, Henry & Antonio Michielan. 2025. Les relations lexicales entre le giziga – tchadique central – et le fulfulde (Cameroun). Afrika und Übersee 98(1): 98–135. doi:10.15460/auue.2025.98.1.332
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK:, PDF p. 7 = printed p. 103, §2.5 'Comparaison des deux systèmes' (extracted text): "Le fulfulde est une langue sans tons, alors que le giziga a deux registres tonals (haut et bas). Nos sources giziga ne notent malheu-reusement pas les tons, sauf à de très rares exceptions." Verbatim; only difference is the line-break hyphen in 'malheureusement'. §2 (pp. 100-103) is a consonant/vowel inventory summary after Shay 2021: 17-28; grep of all four files for accent/stress/prosod/Akzent/Betonung finds nothing about word stress. So the first reader's account of the held files is accurate. WHY THE READING AND STATUS CHANGE: the decisive source, Shay 2021 (Brill, Glottolog MED lon…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for stress placement is given by any source opened. Giziga is described as a two-register tone language (H, L); Njui & Bebey 2021: 226 add a surface Mid tone and HL falling contours. Neither open source mentions word stress or accent at all; the 49-page phonology chapter of Shay 2021 (pp. 17–65), the only full modern description, could not be opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the article's own lexical sources do not mark tone.
new_statements.domain_note: General statement about the language; the article's data are a lexicon (Michielan et al. ms., built on René Jaouen's file for giziga-sud/Muturwa) and its phonology summary follows Shay 2021: 17–28.
new_statements.identity_note: Shay 2021 and Lukas 1970 treat North (Dogba/Maroua, nort3047) and South (Muturwa, sout3051) Giziga as one language, and Glottolog cites Shay 2021 on both pages while listing the dialect 'Muturuwa' [mutu1250] under North Giziga; per Tourneux & Michielan 2025: 98–99 Lukas's description centres on the northern Dogba variety. The tone statement quoted comes from Tourneux & Michielan, whose lexical data derive from René Jaouen's giziga-sud (Muturwa) file and whose phonology summary follows Shay 2021, so it applies to Giziga as a whole rather than specifically to North Giziga. Njui & Bebey 2021 (Univ. of Maroua) do not name their variety.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry & Antonio Michielan. 2025. Les relations lexicales entre le giziga – tchadique central – et le fulfulde (Cameroun). Afrika und Übersee 98(1): 98–135. doi:10.15460/auue.2025.98.1.332
sources.quote: Le fulfulde est une langue sans tons, alors que le giziga a deux registres tonals (haut et bas). Nos sources giziga ne notent malheureusement pas les tons, sauf à de très rares exceptions.
sources.note: §2 'Les systèmes phonologiques du giziga et du fulfulde' (pp. 100–103) gives consonant and vowel inventories after Shay (2021: 17–28) and states on p. 103 that Giziga has two tone registers (high, low); nothing whatsoever on stress or accent. Also states (p. 98) that Lukas 1970, Barreteau & Dieu 2000 and Shay 2021 treat North and South Giziga as one language, and that Lukas's work centred on the Dogba (northern) variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages nort3047 (North Giziga), sout3051 (South Giziga), mutu1250 (Muturuwa dialect); WALS lect giz 'Gisiga'; PHOIBLE inventory 1624 'Gisiga'; Grambank nort3047
sources.note: Database records only: MEDs are Shay 2021 (long grammar), Lukas 1970 (sketch), Strümpell 1922-23 (wordlist); Shay 2021 is cited on both the North and South Giziga pages; Glottolog lists the dialect 'Muturuwa' under North Giziga. No stress datum anywhere.
